summary: The air side of the battle window and a bombing's, which battles have a marker, and the air map mode's icons of finished battles.

structs.name: CWingOption
structs.comment: A row of the `planes` list of an air battle's or a bombing's window, made from the window `wing_option`: a sub unit, a building of the province, or what the province holds or makes of a good. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 13.
structs.evidence: CCombatView::UpdateSide allocates 0x44 bytes for each; the RTTI export gives the table.

addresses.name: CWingOption::CWingOption
addresses.no_signature: The gui in ECX and nine stack arguments: the entry's memory, the province, the province's building or null, the good made or 7, the good held or 7, what the screen's slot 16 answers, the battle, and the sub unit's id in two.
addresses.comment: **A row of a side's `planes` list in the window of an air battle or a bombing**, 0x44 bytes, made from the window `wing_option`. It is one of four things, by what it is given. **A sub unit** (its id at +0x28): `name` is the sub unit's name (its slot 8), `counter_type` takes the sprite `GFX_counter_` + the key of its definition where a sprite of that name exists, `produce` and `pool` are hidden. **A building of the province** (+0x30, a CProvinceBuilding): `name` is the building's name (slot 6 of its definition), `counter_type` takes `icon_build_` + the building's key where there is such a sprite, `produce` and `pool` are hidden. **What the province holds of a good** (+0x38, a good from 0 to 6; 7 is none): `name` is the good's name and `pool` takes the frame good + 1. **What the province makes of a good** (+0x34, likewise): `name` is the good's name and `produce` takes the frame good + 1. For the last two `counter_type` is left as the file gives it. Then CWingOption::Update; the entry's group is `wing_option`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 13.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, 0x72C160; its five callers are all in CCombatView::UpdateSide (0x7335C5, 0x733B2D, 0x733C01, 0x733CB5, 0x733D92).

addresses.name: CWingOption::Update
addresses.comment: Slot 8, what a refresh of the list calls. **For a sub unit**: `str_bar` is strength (+0x5C) * 1000 / its full strength (its slot 12) and `org_bar` organisation (+0x60) * 1000 / the definition's max_organisation (+0xF0), each a whole number of hundredths; `produce` and `pool` hidden. **For a building**: `str_bar` is its present level (+0x24) * 1000 / its built level (+0x20), the same; `org_bar`, `produce` and `pool` hidden. **For a good held**: `str_bar` is the province's pool of it (CMapProvince +0x164 + good * 4) * 1000 / 200000 - full at two hundred; `org_bar` and `produce` hidden. **For a good made**: `str_bar` is what the province makes of it now (+0x270 + good * 4) * 1000 / the most it can make (+0x294 + good * 4); `org_bar` and `pool` hidden. A divisor of nothing gives -1. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 13.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, 0x72C950: the four arms by the sub unit's id resolving, +0x30, +0x38 and +0x34; the literal 200000.

addresses.name: CWingOption::GetSubUnit
addresses.comment: The sub unit a row stands for: FindPersistentById on the id at +0x28, in the table its type belongs to. Null for a row that stands for a building or a good. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 13.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C; the entry in EAX, no stack argument.

addresses.name: CWingOption::IsStillThere
addresses.comment: Whether a row still stands for something. A row whose id (+0x28, +0x2C) is the null id: slot 8 of its building's definition where it has a building (+0x30), and true where it has none - a good's row. Any other: whether the id still names an object. CCombatView::UpdateSide asks it of every row of a bombing's list before it refreshes one. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 13.
addresses.evidence: The listing 0x72E690..0x72E70A: the compare with the null id at 0x1A8CC94, the FindPersistentById, the tail at 0x72E6F0.

addresses.name: CUnitList::SumSubUnitCounts
addresses.comment: The sub unit counts (CUnit +0x40) of every unit of a list, added up. CCombatView::UpdateSide holds the number of rows of an air battle's `planes` list against it, and CCombat::Tick multiplies the two strategic warfare figures of an air battle by it. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 13.

addresses.name: GoodName
addresses.no_signature: The good in ECX and the string to fill in a register that was not pinned; a bare `ret`, so nothing on the stack.
addresses.comment: **A good's name in the player's language**, by its number: the text whose key is the entry of the table at 0x170AF54 - `SUPPLIES_IRO`, `FUEL_IRO`, `MONEY_IRO`, `CRUDE_OIL_IRO`, `METAL_IRO`, `ENERGY_IRO`, `RAREMAT_IRO` for goods 0 to 6 - rendered. The rows of a bombing's list that stand for a good are named by it. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 13.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C; the seven pointers of the table read with their strings.

addresses.name: ShowAirBattleIcon
addresses.signature: void __stdcall ShowAirBattleIcon(void* mapObjects@ECX, void* provinceObject@stack:4, int count@stack:8)
addresses.comment: **The air map mode's icon of an air battle over a province.** With a count above 0 and no icon yet (the province object's +0x68): a billboard of the type `air_battle_icon` (interface/mapitems.gfx) is made, hung on the province, shown, and given the vector (3, 3, 0) through its slot 33. With an icon and a count under 1 it is hidden and destroyed. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 14.
addresses.evidence: Read from the listing 0x642530..0x64268A; the float 3.0 at 0x171DC88; one caller, 0x86A43C.

addresses.name: UpdateAirMapIcons
addresses.comment: **What the air map mode shows of battles: three counts for every province, out of the list of finished battles** (the combat manager's history). For each entry of kind 3 (an air battle) or 4, 5, 6 (a bombing), by its province: where the player owns or controls the province or is the entry's defender, or the entry's defender is a real country other than REB that is on the player's side, or one that exists and is no enemy of the player, a bombing counts as **bombed us** and an air battle as an air battle. Otherwise, where the player is the entry's attacker, or the attacker passes CCountry::CanOperateIn, or the defender is the player's enemy, a bombing counts as **bombed them** and an air battle as an air battle; and an entry that is none of these is left out. Then for every province ShowBombedUsIcon, ShowBombedThemIcon and ShowAirBattleIcon with its three counts. It goes on to two more icons of each land province, by the levels of the buildings at +0x304 and +0x308 - the level itself for a province the player knows well enough (above 1), and otherwise only whether there is one. CInGameIdler::DailyUpdate calls it in map mode 18. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 14.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, 0x86A1E0; three callers (0x661CDB in CInGameIdler::DailyUpdate, 0x66801A, 0x678A20).

addresses.name: CCombatView::UpdateSide
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CCombatView::UpdateSide(CCombatView* view, CCombatant* side, bool attacker, void* sideWindow, bool first)
addresses.comment: **One half of the window.** Land: `committed_label` is COMMITED_LABEL with $COUNT$ the front's count (+0xB8) and $WIDTH$ SumUnitListCombatWidth of the front over 1000; `reserves_label` is RESERVES_LABEL with the reserves' count (+0xC8); the lists `committed` and `reserves` by CCombatView::FillUnitList. Naval: section 12. **An air battle** (kind 3): `planes_label` is the count of the side's sub units (CUnitList::CountSubUnits) in yellow and PLANES_LABEL; the list `planes` is kept while it has as many rows as CUnitList::SumSubUnitCounts and each row's sub unit resolves and is on a unit of the side, and otherwise emptied and filled with a CWingOption for every sub unit of every unit, in the side's order. **A bombing** (slot 8): the attacker's `planes_label` as an air battle's and the defender's empty; the defender's `planes` holds, where the attacker has a unit, a row for every building its first unit's order bombs (slot 30) that the province has built, then for each good a row of what the province holds where the order bombs stockpiles (slot 31) and a row of what it makes where the order bombs production (slot 32) and the province can make any, and then - as the attacker's does alone - a row for every sub unit of every unit of the side; it is filled again when its number of rows is not that number or a row is no longer there (CWingOption::IsStillThere), or when the `first` argument is set. Then for any kind: the highest ranked leader's name and portrait (gfx/pictures/portraits/<picture>.tga in the shape of GFX_empty_position), set when he is another than the one remembered, or NO_COMMANDER for a side with a country and no leader; `shield` given the leader's unit's owner, else the side's first country, else the province's controller; and, for a side with a tactic, `initiative_indicator` shown on the side whose leader has more skill, and `tactic_name` and `tactic_picture` (gfx/pictures/tactics/<picture>.dds in the shape of GFX_empty_tactics, where the file exists) when the tactic is another than the one remembered. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, sections 4, 12 and 13.
addresses.evidence: The air arm is the listing 0x733285..0x73360A and the bombing arm 0x73360F..0x733DCA, read with the decompiled C.
addresses.revises: The air arm and the bombing arm are added; the comment said neither was read.

addresses.name: CCombatView::Update
addresses.comment: **The window's refresh, every frame.** `combat_progress` is the attacker's share (CCombat slot 17) as a whole number from 0 to 100; `combat_width` CCombat::GetCombatWidth over 1000; `combat_attack_indicator`, land only, frame 2 where the attacker's tactic counters the defender's, 3 the other way round, 1 for neither. Then **the modifiers are worked out again for the window** - slot 19 of the attacker with (defender, 1) and of the defender with (attacker, 1). `retreat_button` is enabled by CCombat slot 12. `combat_modifiers` is rebuilt when the number of ids set in either side's modifier_used is not its number of entries: for each id set on either side a `combat_modifier` window whose `combat_mod_icon` takes the sprite CMOD_<key> where one exists. It hides the window and **answers false** - a land battle where a side has no units or a side's two lists are both empty, a naval battle where a side has no units, **an air battle where either side's `planes` list is empty, and a bombing where the attacker's is**, the defender's not being asked; else CCombatView::UpdateSides(0), puts the child `attacker` at `left_pos` and `defender` at `right_pos`, and starts a sound when the last one is over. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: The listing 0x730220..0x730440: slot 8 first, with the child `attacker` alone; then kind 3 with `attacker` and `defender`.
addresses.revises: Which lists take an air battle's window down and which a bombing's.

addresses.name: CCombat::Tick
addresses.comment: **One hour of a combat, and the answer is whether it is over.** CCombat slot 15; the naval and air ticks call it first. In order: CCombat::StampWars; CCombat::PickTactics where a side has none or TACTIC_SWAP_FREQUENCEY divides the duration; `duration` incremented; on the first hour two dice and +0x1C set to 0; **two dice every hour** (`Random() % 10` into each side's +0x50, attacker first); slot 19 (ApplyCombatModifiers) for the attacker and then the defender; slot 15 (Attack) for the attacker and then the defender; a strategic warfare tally; CCombatant::ApplyLosses for each; ships under 0.1 strength removed; and **from the fourth hour**, unless +0x2B is set, `attacker->HasLost()` (slot 16) then `defender->HasLost()` - a loser has CCombat::Conclude and every one of its units CUnit::RetreatFromCombat, and the answer is 1. Otherwise +0x1C is incremented and the answer is 0. The stack argument is never read. The refresh of the status window comes last, in the same block as the two tests of who has lost - so **not before the fourth hour** and never for a convoy battle - and only where slot 8 says the battle is no bombing, its kind is neither 3 nor 2, and the player is among the defender's countries or the attacker's: **the marker on the map is a land battle's alone.** See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landbattle.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, the tail of 0x56EBE0: vf_8, GetKind against 3 and 2, and the two CountryIdListContains before the call at 0x56F34C, which findRefs gives as the one call of CCombat::UpdateCombatStatusWindow in the image.
addresses.revises: When the marker is refreshed and for which battles; reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 12, had the marker for a battle at sea too.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::DailyUpdate
addresses.comment: CInGameIdler virtual slot 53: repaints the map in modes 4/18/19, then always runs the autosave check. Takes nothing on the stack (bare `ret` on all three paths) and returns true - every path sets `al, 1` before the epilogue. The mode is the dword at +0xD34; mode 4 calls MapMode_Supply_Colour (0x266EE0); **mode 0x12, the air mode, calls UpdateAirMapIcons (0x46A1E0) - the icons of the air battles and bombings in the list of finished battles - and then 0x46AD60**; mode 0x13, the naval mode, calls 0x46A6F0; all three on the map object's +0x1DC4. Every path ends with `push esi; call 0x261D20`, the autosave check. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 14.
addresses.revises: Names what mode 18's first call is.
